title: Lost Weapons
paragraphs: I smashed through the gate with ease. That was quite satisfying.
“I did it.”
“…If we were to put it in game terms, it’s like an event where the required stats are enormous, but not impossible to clear.”
“Well, since we managed to shortcut through it, I’d say it’s a win.”
“Yeah. In the end, brute force makes things easier.”
“Oh my, how wonderful.”
“This just shows how strong the heroes are… To be able to break through a barrier of such high density head-on like that is something I’ve never seen before.”
“This was nothing.”
If I had to compare, this was weaker than the barrier used by the creature that came from beyond the wave in the previous loop.
Since it was layered many times over, maybe it was just a bit stronger?
“They should have placed a barrier in the desert as well. Their preparations were sloppy.”
Rival’s remark ruined my moment of triumph.
“What? If it’s a beam battle from my eyes, I won’t lose.”
“Shall we do this?”
I lost last time because of a surprise attack, but this time, I’ll finish him off. As Rival and I glared at each other (with magic vision), Father stepped in to stop us.
“Come on, let’s just check out the inside for now. We don’t know what’s in there.”
“Fair enough.”

And so, we proceeded inside the castle. I have to say, the castle’s interior wasn’t all that different. It was an extremely old structure, and parts of it were clearly in ruins. There must have been bones scattered around before, but they had completely disintegrated with time.
“Some places are buried in sand.”
“There are also areas that have collapsed. And… there are doors that look like no one’s opened them since they were first sealed.”
“Yet despite that, demons are lurking inside… Did they teleport in?”
“Who knows?”

With that conversation, we moved toward the direction where the demons seemed to be concentrated. According to Father, in situations like this, you should always head in the direction the enemy doesn’t want you to go. Following that logic, we reached a courtyard-like area where water had gathered to form a spring, creating a place of respite. Near the edge of the spring… were the remnants of a familiar-looking monument and what appeared to be a destroyed inscription.
“Is that…?”
“It looks like the same inscriptions from the Dracia Mountains and Cal Mira Island. Were they destroyed here too?”
“Which means… this place is another activated region.”
“How’s everyone’s experience gain?”
“Demon experience points aren’t very rewarding.”
The big sisters nodded at Ren’s words.
“I see… For now, let’s take a closer look at the inscription.”
“Indeed.”

We approached the inscription and tried to read the characters written on it. …There were clear signs that someone had tried to scrape it off multiple times. As we drew closer, the gems embedded in our weapons began to glow, and the text started to emerge.
“Does this mean the demons didn’t want anyone to read it?”
“Possibly. Hmm… As I thought, it seems to describe the Liberation magic here. But… there’s more written.”

I also read the text. Let’s see… Fixed Pseudo-Liberation Absorb… To step into a higher realm, combine the power of the heroes and weave together the two magics… That’s what it seems to say. It also mentions that the method involves a blessing from the dragon. We’ve already obtained that. But if this was the only hint, then the fact that Father reached Liberation in the first world with no hints at all makes him a magical genius.
“A rank of magic that’s above Dryfe, but below true Liberation…”
“A trial version of Liberation, huh.”
“I’m not sure how I feel about that, but it seems accurate. In famous games, it’s like the middle tier between Ra, Da, and Ga-level spells.”
“The standard for famous games… Well, I sort of get it. I’ve only dabbled in those games myself.”
“So, they have that in your world too, Itsuki?”
“What are you talking about? Isn’t it more like Mega, Giga, Omega, and Tera, where this is the Omega-tier? In Makai Daichi, that’s how it was.”
“Depends on the game… but yeah, something like that, I suppose.”
Ren’s reaction was slow.
Was he not following the conversation? That’s what I thought, but it seems he just couldn’t get a word in. He was silently nodding along.
“Signs that someone tried to destroy it multiple times… I’ve heard stories of reincarnators and world transfer cases, so it’s highly likely this was sabotage by someone claiming to be a god.”
“Yeah. From the wave’s side, they thoroughly eliminate anything that might be a threat.”
“Well, either way, it was meaningless in the face of Motoyasu, who keeps looping. Let’s move on.”
While Father and the others were analyzing the situation, the big sisters and the Filolials were resting by the spring. Since we took care of any approaching demons, they had nothing to worry about.
“Sniff sniff… I smell treasure. Gaelion’s instincts are telling me to go this way.”
“Well, it’s not really a detour, but should we check it out? Even if we want to find a way out, we’ll have to go there eventually.”
“Yeah. I’m interested in the treasure.”
“It’s just a gamer’s instinct.”

As we left the courtyard and proceeded toward the area with more demon guards, we discovered a heavily sealed door. Standing guard were towering… multi-winged demons known as Belial, with several of them stationed there. Of course, they were no match for us in our fully powered-up state. Even if it was pseudo, Father cast Liberation-class support magic, and we wiped them out in seconds.
Hahaha! They were nothing but trash.
“There’s more here.”
The door was also tightly sealed, but we broke through it along with the barrier. Beyond that was another door, and this time, it was the rival who, being well-versed in magic, dispelled the seal.
“Piece of cake compared to domain destruction.”

Licking her lips, the rival broke the seal and opened the door. That expression… she was a dragon completely driven by instinct. I was reminded of the scene from the first world where the male version of the rival dove straight into the mountain of treasure Father brought back.
“What’s inside? Gaelion’s instincts are telling me there’s a ton of stuff hidden in this castle!”
Humming cheerfully, I lit up the room. And what we saw left us speechless.
“Wh-What is this!?”
“Whoa…”
“This is…”

Inside, an assortment of weapons was scattered around so casually that the word ‘neglected’ fit perfectly. There were swords, spears, bows, guns, staves, claws, axes, whips… even a carriage. Of course, there were shields too.
Was this some kind of treasury? I appraised the items.

Uniformly… these weapons all had the indestructible attribute. That said, while they were indestructible, they didn’t seem to possess the same level of performance as the heroes’ weapons. Many of the blades were chipped. They weren’t broken, but they had definitely deteriorated over time.
“C-Could these be… the legendary weapons lost in past battles!?”
Even the doctor was unusually surprised.
Lost legendary weapons, huh?
“Is that true?”
In response to Father’s question, we each examined the weapons and nodded.
“It’s like a collection of legendary weapons from games.”
“Yeah, even rare weapons that bosses drop are mixed in here.”
The sanctuary of the Filolials had similar things lying around, but the amount of weapons stored here was beyond comparison.
“A mountain of treasure!”
The rival’s eyes had turned into gold coins. She was completely blinded by greed.
“If you’re a hero, why don’t you try picking up the corresponding weapon?”
